blurb.en: Learn topic words, describing words, bigger and the biggest, and countable nouns.
blurb.vi: Học từ vựng theo chủ đề, từ miêu tả, so sánh hơn, so sánh nhất và danh từ đếm được.

title.vi: Cộng đồng và ngôi nhà của chúng ta

neighbourhood.def: The streets and homes around the place where you live.
neighbourhood.ex: There is a small sports club in our *neighbourhood*.

caretaker.vi: người trông coi và sửa chữa ở trường
caretaker.def: A person who looks after a school building and fixes things.
caretaker.ex: The *caretaker* fixed the broken door of our classroom.

librarian.def: A person who works with books and helps you find the right one.
librarian.ex: The *librarian* helped me find a book about the sea.

chimney.def: A tall pipe on a roof. Smoke from a fire goes out of it.
chimney.ex: Grey smoke came out of the *chimney* on the roof.

bungalow.def: A house with only one floor, so there are no stairs inside.
bungalow.ex: My grandparents live in a *bungalow*, so they don't climb any stairs.

orbit.def: The path a planet or moon takes around something, again and again.
orbit.ex: The Moon moves in an *orbit* around the Earth.

satellite.def: A machine in space that goes around the Earth and sends us pictures.
satellite.ex: A *satellite* takes photos of the clouds for the weather report.

nutritious.def: Full of good things that help your body grow and stay healthy.
nutritious.ex: Fish and green vegetables are *nutritious* foods.

soil.def: The brown earth on the ground where plants grow.
soil.ex: Worms live under the ground in the *soil*.

freezing.def: Very, very cold, like ice and snow.
freezing.ex: It is *freezing* at the top of the mountain, so wear a warm hat.

wooden.def: Made from the hard part of a tree.
wooden.ex: There is a big *wooden* table in our kitchen.

spiky.def: Covered with sharp points that can hurt your fingers.
spiky.ex: A pineapple has *spiky* leaves on top.

juicy.def: Full of sweet water that runs out when you bite it.
juicy.ex: This *juicy* watermelon is perfect on a hot day.

keen.def: Very interested in something and wanting to do it a lot.
keen.ex: Minh is *keen* on skateboarding. He practises every day.

title.vi: So sánh hơn và so sánh nhất

scenes.head: A page from a space book for children
scenes.html: There are eight planets in our Solar System. Mars is *smaller* than Earth. Earth is *bigger* than Mars, but Jupiter is *the biggest* planet of all. Mercury is *the smallest* planet. It is *closer* to the Sun than Earth. Venus is *hotter* than Mercury. It is *the hottest* planet! Saturn has got big rings. Some people say it is *the most beautiful* planet.

steps.en: Look at the words in gold. We use them to compare things.
steps.vi: Hãy nhìn các từ màu vàng. Chúng ta dùng chúng để so sánh các vật.

steps.en: Two things? Add *-er* and use *than*: Mars is *smaller than* Earth.
steps.vi: So sánh hai vật? Thêm *-er* và dùng *than*: Mars is *smaller than* Earth.

steps.en: One of a big group? Use *the* and *-est*: Jupiter is *the biggest* planet.
steps.vi: So sánh một vật với cả nhóm? Dùng *the* và *-est*: Jupiter is *the biggest* planet.

steps.en: Long words use *more* and *the most*: *the most beautiful* planet.
steps.vi: Từ dài dùng *more* và *the most*: *the most beautiful* planet.

title.vi: Good, better, the best: so sánh đặc biệt

scenes.head: Ruby's football club diary
scenes.html: My football club played three matches this month. The first match was *good*. We scored one goal. The second match was *better*. We scored three goals! The last match was *the best* because we won the cup. But the weather was a problem. It was *bad* on the first day and *worse* on the second day. On the last day it was *the worst*: cold, wet and windy!

steps.en: Some describing words don't add *-er* or *-est*. They change into new words.
steps.vi: Một số từ miêu tả không thêm *-er* hay *-est*. Chúng đổi thành từ mới.

steps.en: Say them like a little song: good, better, best; bad, worse, worst.
steps.vi: Hãy đọc như một bài hát nhỏ: good, better, best; bad, worse, worst.

title.vi: Danh từ đếm được và không đếm được

scenes.head: A note from Dad on the fridge
scenes.html:
Theo, please go to the shop for me. We need *six eggs*, *a cabbage* and *two mangoes*. We also need *some rice* and *some cheese*. Please buy *a bottle of* water and *a loaf of* bread too. Thank you!
Love, Dad

steps.en: *Eggs* and *mangoes* are countable. We can count them: one egg, two mangoes.
steps.vi: *Eggs* và *mangoes* là danh từ đếm được. Ta đếm được: one egg, two mangoes.

steps.en: *Rice*, *cheese*, *water* and *bread* are uncountable. We say *some rice*, with no *-s*.
steps.vi: *Rice*, *cheese*, *water* và *bread* là danh từ không đếm được. Ta nói *some rice*, không thêm *-s*.

steps.en: Use *a* or *an* only for ONE countable thing: *a* cabbage, *an* egg.
steps.vi: Chỉ dùng *a* hoặc *an* cho MỘT vật đếm được: *a* cabbage, *an* egg.

steps.en: To count uncountable things, use a container: *a bottle of* water, *a loaf of* bread.
steps.vi: Muốn đếm vật không đếm được, hãy dùng từ chỉ vật chứa: *a bottle of* water, *a loaf of* bread.

end.en: Great work! You found the special words in all three texts.
end.vi: Làm tốt lắm! Em đã tìm được các từ đặc biệt trong cả ba bài đọc.

challenge.result: You spotted bigger and the biggest, better and the best, and countable and uncountable nouns.

v.q: Jupiter is ________ planet of all.
whys: Bigger is for two things, with than. Here Jupiter is one of all the planets.
Big does not compare. The words 'of all' tell you to compare.
v.hint: Look at 'of all'. Is Jupiter compared with one planet or with all of them?
v.worked: Jupiter is compared with all the planets, so we need *the biggest*: 'the biggest planet of all'.

v.q: Mars is ________ than Earth.
whys: We use the smallest for one of a big group, not with than.
Small does not compare. Look at the word than.
v.hint: Look at the word after the gap. Which form goes with than?
v.worked: We compare two planets with *than*, so we add -er: 'Mars is *smaller* than Earth.'

v.q: The last match was ________ because we won the cup.
whys: The worst doesn't make sense. Ruby's club won the cup!
Better compares two things. Ruby is talking about all three matches.
v.hint: Ruby played three matches. Was the last one compared with one match or with all of them?
v.worked: It was the top match of all three, so it was *the best*: 'we won the cup'.

v.q: The weather was bad on day one and ________ on day two.
whys: The worst is for the very last day, the most terrible one of all.
Bad is day one. Day two was more bad than that.
v.hint: Day two is compared with day one only. Which form compares two days?
v.worked: Bad becomes *worse* when we compare two days: 'bad on day one and *worse* on day two'.

v.q: We also need ________ rice.
whys: We use an with one countable thing, like an egg. We can't count rice.
We can't count rice, so we can't say a number before it.
v.hint: Can you count rice grain by grain in a shop? Is rice countable or uncountable?
v.worked: Rice is uncountable, so Dad writes *some rice*.

v.q: Please buy a ________ of water.
whys: We use a loaf for bread, not water.
We use a slice for bread or cake. Water is a drink.
v.hint: Water is a drink. What do we put water in at the shop?
v.worked: We buy water in *a bottle*: 'a bottle of water'.

v.q: Some people say Saturn is ________ planet.
whys: More beautiful compares two things, with than.
Beautiful does not compare. Saturn is compared with all the planets.
v.hint: Beautiful is a long word. Which form compares one planet with all the others?
v.worked: Long words use *the most* for one of a group: 'the most beautiful planet'.

v.q: Mercury is ________ to the Sun than Earth.
whys: The closest is for one of a big group, not with than.
Close does not compare. Look for the word than.
v.hint: Find the word than in the sentence. Which form goes with it?
v.worked: Two planets are compared with *than*, so we need *closer*: 'closer to the Sun than Earth'.

blurb.en: One step at a time: topic words, bigger and the biggest, and a, an or some.
blurb.vi: Từng bước một: từ vựng chủ đề, so sánh hơn, so sánh nhất và a, an hay some.

title.vi: Từ vựng của bốn chủ đề

v.q: Who looks after the school building and fixes broken things?
whys: The librarian works with books, not broken doors.
The cook makes lunch in the school kitchen.
v.hint: Think about the people at school. Who has tools to mend things?
v.worked: The *caretaker* looks after the building and fixes things.

v.q: Who works with books and helps you find one to read?
whys: The school nurse helps you when you are ill or hurt.
The head teacher is the leader of the whole school.
v.hint: Where are the books at school? Who works there?
v.worked: The *librarian* works in the library and helps you find books.

v.q: A house with only one floor and no stairs is a ________.
whys: A chimney is a pipe on the roof for smoke.
A balcony is a small place outside a window, high up.
v.hint: The sentence talks about a whole house. Which word is a kind of home?
v.worked: A *bungalow* is a house with one floor: 'only one floor and no stairs'.

v.q: A machine in space that goes around the Earth is a ________.
whys: A planet is not a machine. People don't make planets.
A sunset is when the Sun goes down in the evening.
v.hint: Find the word machine. Which one do people make and send into space?
v.worked: A *satellite* is a machine that goes around the Earth.

v.q: Make a describing word from wood. Type it.
lines: This table is made of wood. It is a {0} table.
v.hint: Think of 'gold' and 'golden'. Which ending makes a describing word?
v.worked: Wood + en = *wooden*: 'a wooden table'.

v.q: Make a describing word from juice. Type it.
lines: This watermelon is full of juice. It is very {0}.
v.hint: Think of 'salt' and 'salty'. Which ending makes a describing word? Check the spelling.
v.worked: Juice + y = *juicy*: the e goes. 'It is very juicy.'

title.vi: So sánh hơn và so sánh nhất

v.q: An elephant is ________ than a dog.
whys: Biggest is for one of a big group, with the. Here we see than.
Big does not compare two animals.
v.hint: Look for the word than. How many animals are we comparing?
v.worked: Two animals with *than*: big + g + er = *bigger*.

v.q: A train is ________ than a bike.
whys: Fastest is for one of a big group, with the.
Fast does not compare. Look at the word than.
v.hint: We compare two things here. Which form goes with than?
v.worked: Two things with *than*, so we add -er: 'faster than a bike'.

v.q: Fansipan is ________ mountain in Vietnam.
whys: Higher compares two mountains, with than.
High does not compare. Fansipan is compared with all the mountains in Vietnam.
v.hint: Is Fansipan compared with one mountain or with all the mountains in Vietnam?
v.worked: It is the top one of all the mountains in Vietnam, so we say *the highest*.

v.q: This is ________ book in the library. It has 900 pages!
whys: Longer compares two books, with than.
Long does not compare. The book is compared with all the books in the library.
v.hint: Look at 'in the library'. Is the book compared with one book or all of them?
v.worked: One book compared with all the books in the library: *the longest* book.

v.q: Type the missing word.
lines: The weather was bad on Monday. On Tuesday it was {0}. It rained all day!
v.hint: Bad is a special word. It does not add -er. Say the little song: bad, ..., worst.
v.worked: Bad → *worse* → the worst. Tuesday was *worse* than Monday.

v.q: Type the missing word.
lines: Linh's drawing is good, but Jade's drawing is {0}.
v.hint: Good is a special word. It does not add -er. Say the little song: good, ..., best.
v.worked: Good → *better* → the best. Jade's drawing is *better*.

title.vi: Đếm được hay không đếm được?

v.q: Which word is uncountable?
whys: We can count eggs: one egg, two eggs.
We can count mangoes: one mango, two mangoes.
v.hint: Try to say 'two ...' before each word. Which one sounds wrong?
v.worked: We can't say 'two rices'. *Rice* is uncountable: some rice.

v.q: Which word is countable?
whys: Bread is uncountable. We say some bread or a loaf of bread.
Water is uncountable. We say some water or a glass of water.
v.hint: Try to say 'three ...' before each word. Which one sounds right?
v.worked: We can say one carrot, three carrots. *Carrot* is countable.

v.q: Can I have ________ water, please?
whys: We use a with one countable thing. Water is uncountable.
We use an with one countable thing, like an egg. Water is uncountable.
v.hint: Is water countable or uncountable?
v.worked: Water is uncountable, so we say *some water*.

v.q: I eat ________ egg every morning.
whys: Egg starts with a vowel sound, e. We don't say a before it.
Many is for more than one, like many eggs, with -s.
v.hint: Look at egg: one thing, with no -s. How does the word egg start?
v.worked: One egg, and egg starts with a vowel sound, so we say *an egg*.

v.q: Mum bought a ________ of bread.
whys: A bottle is for drinks, like water or juice.
A glass is for drinks, like milk.
v.hint: Bread is not a drink. What do we call a whole piece of bread from the shop?
v.worked: We buy bread as *a loaf of bread*.

v.q: Would you like a ________ of milk?
whys: A slice is a thin piece of bread or cake.
A loaf is for bread.
v.hint: Milk is a drink. What do we drink it from?
v.worked: We drink milk from a glass: *a glass of milk*.

blurb.en: Like the real Reading paper: circle the right word and fill the gaps in a story.
blurb.vi: Giống bài thi Đọc thật: khoanh từ đúng và điền vào chỗ trống trong câu chuyện.

title.en: Reading Part 3: circle the topic word
title.vi: Đọc Phần 3: khoanh từ vựng đúng

v.q: The ________ gave me a plaster when I hurt my knee.
whys: The caretaker fixes the school building, not hurt knees.
The librarian helps you with books.
v.hint: Find the words 'hurt my knee'. Who helps children when they are hurt?
v.worked: The *school nurse* helps when you are hurt: 'gave me a plaster'.

v.q: We made a ________ to tell people about our charity fair.
whys: A sandpit is a place with sand where small children play.
A surgery is where you go to see a doctor.
v.hint: Which thing has words on it that tell people about an event?
v.worked: A *leaflet* is a small paper that tells people about something: 'to tell people about our charity fair'.

v.q: At night, the stars in a ________ make a picture in the sky.
whys: A sunset happens in the evening. It is not made of stars.
A rover is a machine that drives on another planet.
v.hint: Look for 'stars' and 'make a picture'. Which word is a group of stars?
v.worked: A *constellation* is a group of stars that makes a picture.

v.q: The ________ drove slowly over the red rocks on Mars.
whys: A satellite goes around a planet. It doesn't drive on rocks.
Mars is a planet. A planet can't drive.
v.hint: Look at the verb drove. Which thing has wheels?
v.worked: A *rover* is a space machine that drives: 'drove slowly over the red rocks'.

v.q: The smoke from the fire went up the ________.
whys: A balcony is outside a window. Smoke doesn't go up it.
The floor is at the bottom of a room. Smoke can't go up it.
v.hint: Look at 'smoke' and 'went up'. Which part of a house is a tall pipe?
v.worked: Smoke goes up the *chimney* and out through the roof.

v.q: Dad put the nuts in a hot oven to ________ them.
whys: To rinse is to wash something in water, not in an oven.
To fold is to bend paper or clothes. You can't fold nuts.
v.hint: Look at 'a hot oven'. What do we do to food in a hot oven?
v.worked: We *roast* food in a hot oven: 'put the nuts in a hot oven to roast them'.

title.en: Reading Part 3: circle the right form
title.vi: Đọc Phần 3: khoanh dạng từ đúng

v.q: My brother is two, so he is ________ than me.
whys: Youngest is for one of a big group, with the.
Young does not compare. Look at the word than.
v.hint: Look at the word than. How many people are we comparing?
v.worked: Two people with *than*, so we add -er: 'younger than me'.

v.q: Our new classroom has big windows. It is ________ than the old one.
whys: Brightest is for one of a big group, with the.
Bright does not compare two rooms.
v.hint: Two classrooms are compared. Which form goes with than?
v.worked: We compare two rooms with *than*: 'brighter than the old one'.

v.q: Kai loves football. He thinks it is ________ sport in the world.
whys: The worst doesn't make sense. Kai loves football!
Better compares two things, with than. Football is compared with every sport.
v.hint: Read the first sentence. Then look at 'in the world'. Is football compared with one sport or all of them?
v.worked: Kai loves football, and it is compared with all sports, so it is *the best* sport.

v.q: I didn't like the film at all. It was ________ film of the year.
whys: Worse compares two films, with than.
Bad does not compare. Look at 'of the year'.
v.hint: Look at 'of the year'. Is it one of a big group?
v.worked: The film is compared with all the films of the year: *the worst* film.

v.q: How ________ sugar do we need for the cake?
whys: We use many with countable nouns, like many eggs. Sugar is uncountable.
We don't say a with uncountable nouns like sugar.
v.hint: Is sugar countable or uncountable?
v.worked: Sugar is uncountable, so we ask *How much sugar?*

v.q: How ________ eggs are there in the box?
whys: We use much with uncountable nouns, like much sugar. Eggs are countable.
A is for one thing. Eggs has -s, so there is more than one.
v.hint: Look at eggs. Can you count them?
v.worked: Eggs are countable, so we ask *How many eggs?*

title.en: Reading Part 4: a story with gaps
title.vi: Đọc Phần 4: câu chuyện có chỗ trống

v.q: Read Kai's story. Choose the word for gap (1).
whys: A sandpit is a place to play. You can't give one to every family.
A surgery is a building where doctors work.
v.hint: Read the next sentence. What can you give to every family in a street?
v.worked: 'We gave one to every family in our street.' So they made a *leaflet*.

stim.head: Kai's story
stim.html:
Our neighbourhood fun run
by Kai

Last Saturday there was a fun run in our neighbourhood. We wanted to raise money for our sports club. My friend Hugo and I made a (1) ________ about the run. We gave one to every family in our street.

On the day it was hot and (2) ________. The air felt very wet, so everyone drank lots of water.

Hugo has got long legs. He is (3) ________ than me, so he finished first. I finished fifth, and I was very happy. We raised a lot of money for new footballs!

v.q: Read Zara's story. Choose the word for gap (1).
whys: A is for one thing. Grapes has -s, so there are more than one.
Much is for uncountable things. We can count grapes.
v.hint: Look at the word after the gap. Is it one thing or more than one?
v.worked: Grapes are countable and plural, so we say *some grapes*.

stim.head: Zara's story
stim.html:
Fruit salad with Grandpa
by Zara

On Sunday I made a fruit salad with Grandpa. Fruit is very nutritious, and it is delicious too!

First we washed two mangoes, a papaya and (1) ________ grapes. Then Grandpa cut the pineapple for me. It has (2) ________ skin and leaves, and they can hurt your fingers.

We put all the fruit in a big bowl with some yoghurt on top. Mum tasted it and smiled. 'This is (3) ________ than the fruit salad from the shop!' she said. Now it is my favourite snack.

v.q: Read Kai's story. Choose the word for gap (2).
whys: Freezing means very cold, but the story says it was hot.
Icy means cold, like ice. The story says it was hot.
v.hint: Read the sentence after the gap. How did the air feel?
v.worked: 'The air felt very wet', and it was hot. Hot, wet air is *humid*.

stim.head: Kai's story
stim.html:
Our neighbourhood fun run
by Kai

Last Saturday there was a fun run in our neighbourhood. We wanted to raise money for our sports club. My friend Hugo and I made a (1) ________ about the run. We gave one to every family in our street.

On the day it was hot and (2) ________. The air felt very wet, so everyone drank lots of water.

Hugo has got long legs. He is (3) ________ than me, so he finished first. I finished fifth, and I was very happy. We raised a lot of money for new footballs!

v.q: Read Zara's story. Choose the word for gap (2).
whys: Juicy is about the fruit inside. Juicy things don't hurt you.
Smooth things are soft to touch. They don't hurt you.
v.hint: Read the end of the sentence. What can the skin and leaves do to you?
v.worked: 'They can hurt your fingers.' So the pineapple has *spiky* skin and leaves.

stim.head: Zara's story
stim.html:
Fruit salad with Grandpa
by Zara

On Sunday I made a fruit salad with Grandpa. Fruit is very nutritious, and it is delicious too!

First we washed two mangoes, a papaya and (1) ________ grapes. Then Grandpa cut the pineapple for me. It has (2) ________ skin and leaves, and they can hurt your fingers.

We put all the fruit in a big bowl with some yoghurt on top. Mum tasted it and smiled. 'This is (3) ________ than the fruit salad from the shop!' she said. Now it is my favourite snack.

v.q: Read Kai's story. Choose the word for gap (3).
whys: Fastest is for one of a big group, with the. Here we see than.
Slower doesn't make sense. Hugo finished first!
v.hint: Read the end of the sentence. Who finished first?
v.worked: Hugo 'finished first', so he is *faster* than Kai.

stim.head: Kai's story
stim.html:
Our neighbourhood fun run
by Kai

Last Saturday there was a fun run in our neighbourhood. We wanted to raise money for our sports club. My friend Hugo and I made a (1) ________ about the run. We gave one to every family in our street.

On the day it was hot and (2) ________. The air felt very wet, so everyone drank lots of water.

Hugo has got long legs. He is (3) ________ than me, so he finished first. I finished fifth, and I was very happy. We raised a lot of money for new footballs!

v.q: Read Zara's story. Choose the word for gap (3).
whys: Best is for one of a big group, with the. Here we see than.
Good does not compare. Look at the word than.
v.hint: Look at the word than after the gap. Good is a special word.
v.worked: Good → *better* → the best. 'This is better than the fruit salad from the shop!'

stim.head: Zara's story
stim.html:
Fruit salad with Grandpa
by Zara

On Sunday I made a fruit salad with Grandpa. Fruit is very nutritious, and it is delicious too!

First we washed two mangoes, a papaya and (1) ________ grapes. Then Grandpa cut the pineapple for me. It has (2) ________ skin and leaves, and they can hurt your fingers.

We put all the fruit in a big bowl with some yoghurt on top. Mum tasted it and smiled. 'This is (3) ________ than the fruit salad from the shop!' she said. Now it is my favourite snack.

items.en: Short describing words: add *-er* + *than* for two things, and *the ... -est* for one of a group.
items.vi: Từ miêu tả ngắn: thêm *-er* + *than* khi so sánh hai vật, và dùng *the ... -est* cho một vật trong cả nhóm.
example: A bus is *bigger than* a car.
The blue whale is *the biggest* animal.

items.en: Watch the spelling: *big → bigger*, *hot → hotter*, *nice → nicer*, *funny → funnier*.
items.vi: Chú ý chính tả: *big → bigger*, *hot → hotter*, *nice → nicer*, *funny → funnier*.
example: My cat is *funnier* than my dog.

items.en: Long describing words use *more* and *the most*.
items.vi: Từ miêu tả dài dùng *more* và *the most*.
example: This book is *more interesting* than that one.
It's *the most beautiful* beach on the island.

items.en: Two special words: *good, better, the best* and *bad, worse, the worst*.
items.vi: Hai từ đặc biệt: *good, better, the best* và *bad, worse, the worst*.
example: My drawing is *better* than last week.
That was *the worst* storm of the year.

items.en: Countable nouns take *a / an*, *-s* and *many*. Uncountable nouns take *some* or *much*, with no *a* and no *-s*.
items.vi: Danh từ đếm được đi với *a / an*, thêm *-s* và dùng *many*. Danh từ không đếm được đi với *some* hoặc *much*, không có *a* và không thêm *-s*.

items.en: To count uncountable things, use a container or a piece: *a bottle of*, *a glass of*, *a loaf of*, *a slice of*, *a bowl of*.
items.vi: Muốn đếm vật không đếm được, dùng từ chỉ vật chứa hoặc miếng: *a bottle of*, *a glass of*, *a loaf of*, *a slice of*, *a bowl of*.
example: I eat *a bowl of* rice for lunch.
Can I have *two slices of* bread?

check.sentence: A whale is {bigger|biggest|big} than a shark.
This is the {most beautiful|more beautiful|beautiful} flower in the garden.
Jade's cake is {better|best|good} than my cake.
Would you like a {glass|loaf|slice} of milk?

v.q: Minh is very ________ on skateboarding. He practises in his street every evening.
whys: Freezing means very cold. It is about the weather, not people.
Wooden means made of wood. Minh is a boy!
v.hint: Look at the word on after the gap and 'practises every evening'. Which word goes with on?
v.worked: We say *keen on* something when we like it a lot: 'He practises every evening'.

v.q: In winter the lake is ________. You can walk on the ice!
whys: Humid means hot and wet. Ice can't be humid.
Juicy is for fruit with a lot of juice inside.
v.hint: Read the next sentence. What is on the lake?
v.worked: 'You can walk on the ice!' So the lake is very cold: *freezing*.

v.q: Fish and green vegetables are ________. They help you grow strong.
whys: Spiky means covered with sharp points. Most fish aren't spiky.
Salty is about taste. It doesn't help you grow strong.
v.hint: Read the next sentence. What does this food do for your body?
v.worked: 'They help you grow strong.' So the food is *nutritious*.

v.q: My grandparents' house has only one floor. It's a ________.
whys: A chimney is a pipe on a roof, not a whole house.
A balcony is a small place outside a window, not a whole house.
v.hint: The sentence is about a whole house. Which word is a kind of home?
v.worked: A house with 'only one floor' is a *bungalow*.

v.q: Fansipan is ________ mountain in Vietnam.
whys: Higher compares two mountains, with than.
High does not compare. Look at 'in Vietnam'.
v.hint: Is Fansipan compared with one mountain or with all the mountains in Vietnam?
v.worked: Fansipan is the top one of all the mountains in Vietnam: *the highest*.

v.q: A cheetah is ________ than a horse.
whys: The fastest is for one of a big group, not with than.
Fast does not compare. Look at the word than.
v.hint: Look at the word than. How many animals are compared?
v.worked: Two animals with *than*: 'faster than a horse'.

v.q: Hugo had a cold. Today he feels ________ than yesterday, so he can go to school.
whys: The best is for one of a big group, not with than.
Good does not compare. Look at the word than.
v.hint: Look at the word than. Good is a special word.
v.worked: Good → *better* → the best. 'He feels better than yesterday.'

v.q: Jade got ten out of ten. She got ________ mark in the class.
whys: The worst doesn't make sense. Ten out of ten is a very good mark!
Better compares two people, with than. Look at 'in the class'.
v.hint: Look at 'in the class'. Is Jade compared with one child or with everyone?
v.worked: Jade is compared with the whole class, so she got *the best* mark.

v.q: Please buy a ________ of bread for breakfast.
whys: A glass is for drinks, like milk or juice.
A bottle is for drinks, like water.
v.hint: Bread is not a drink. What do we call a whole bread from the shop?
v.worked: We buy *a loaf of bread*.

v.q: How ________ rice do you want?
whys: Many is for countable nouns, like many eggs. Rice is uncountable.
We don't use a with uncountable nouns like rice.
v.hint: Is rice countable or uncountable?
v.worked: Rice is uncountable, so we ask *How much rice?*

v.q: Read Felix's story. Choose the word for gap (6).
whys: Humid means hot and wet. They wouldn't need thick coats.
If the air was warm, they wouldn't need thick coats and hats.
v.hint: Read the end of the sentence. What did the family wear?
v.worked: 'We wore our thick coats and hats.' So the air was very cold: *freezing*.

stim.head: Felix's story
stim.html:
Stars over Grandpa's farm
by Felix

Last month my family stayed at Grandpa's farm. It is far from the city, so the sky is very dark at night.

After dinner we lay on a blanket outside. The air was (6) ________, so we wore our thick coats and hats.

Grandpa showed me a (7) ________. Its stars make the shape of a big spoon.

Then I saw a small light. It moved slowly across the sky. Dad said it was a (8) ________ going around the Earth.

Venus was very bright too. It was (9) ________ than all the stars around it.

whys: A door is in the wall, not the top of a house.
A window is in the wall, not the top of a house.
v.hint: Everything is upside down. Which part is usually at the top, opposite the floor?
v.worked: In a normal house the *roof* is at the top. Here 'the floor was high above our heads', so the roof was on the ground.
